core_obligations: Observe that the principality of I_i(M^bullet, f) implies the same for I_i(N^bullet, f) by the well-definedness lemma, so that the statement is meaningful (proof lines 28173-28176).

Reduce, as in the proof of the well-definedness lemma, to the case N^bullet = M^bullet oplus Q^bullet for the trivial complex Q^bullet concentrated in degrees j and j+1 with differential the identity (proof lines 28177-28182).
Use the compatibility of eta_f with direct sums to see that the displayed map (1, d^i) is the direct sum of the corresponding maps for M^bullet and for Q^bullet (proof lines 28183-28189).
Apply the universal property defining the ideals to conclude J_i(N^bullet, f) = J_i(M^bullet, f) + J_i(Q^bullet, f) (proof lines 28190-28192).
Conclude that it suffices to show J_i(Q^bullet, f) = 0 for all i, a computation the author states is omitted (proof lines 28193-28194).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A, a nonzerodivisor f, and two bounded complexes M^bullet and N^bullet of finite free A-modules representing the same object of D(A), assumes that each I_i(M^bullet, f) is a principal ideal, and concludes that J_i(M^bullet, f) = J_i(N^bullet, f) as ideals of A/fA (source lines 28163-28171). The proof first remarks that the principality of I_i(M^bullet, f) implies the same for I_i(N^bullet, f) by the well-definedness lemma, so that the statement makes sense (proof lines 28173-28176). It then follows the same reduction as in the proof of that lemma: after localization and induction one may assume N^bullet = M^bullet oplus Q^bullet for a trivial complex Q^bullet concentrated in degrees j and j+1 with differential the identity (proof lines 28177-28182). The substantive step uses that eta_f is compatible with direct sums: the map (1, d^i) : (eta_f N)^i / f(eta_f N)^i -> f^i N^i / f^{i+1} N^i oplus f^{i+1} N^{i+1} / f^{i+2} N^{i+1} is then the direct sum of the corresponding maps for M^bullet and for Q^bullet (proof lines 28183-28189). By the universal property defining the ideals in question, this gives J_i(N^bullet, f) = J_i(M^bullet, f) + J_i(Q^bullet, f), so it remains to show J_i(Q^bullet, f) = 0 for all i, a computation the author states is omitted (proof lines 28190-28194). The non-routine content is the direct-sum compatibility that reduces the comparison to the trivial summand.
